claims.statement: The client-side cart is persisted in localStorage, supports items from multiple stores, and is best-effort mirrored for signed-in users; checkout partitions submitted items by `loja_id` and creates one independent order per store without a cross-store rollback.

`finalizarCompra` requires an authenticated user, applies a five-per-minute per-user checkout limit, verifies Turnstile, validates cart/payment input shape, and repeats server-side eligibility checks for Mercado Futuro and perishable-product acceptances before creating orders.

The authenticated `SECURITY DEFINER` `checkout_criar_pedido` RPC is the authoritative order transaction: it locks and validates products/store/quantities/stock, calculates authoritative prices and freight, inserts an `Aguardando Pagamento` order and line items, records platform/affiliate allocation fields, and decrements stock.

Checkout supports PIX, boleto, and credit-card billing; Asaas charge creation uses the authoritative order amount and order ID as `externalReference`, while hosted invoice URLs keep card data outside the application.

Charge creation is intentionally best-effort after durable order creation and uses conditional charge-ID persistence to prevent duplicate live charges under concurrent attempts; a losing attempt tries to cancel its gateway charge, and buyers can retry charge generation only for their own order.

The freight quote endpoint requires a signed-in, rate-limited buyer, prefers an imported carrier-table quote then internal coverage, and calls/persists an Uber Direct quote only when no internal option applies; an Uber quote is later validated as store-owned and unexpired by the order RPC.

The Asaas webhook authenticates with a constant-time token comparison and, for paid events, accepts payment only when both the stored charge ID matches and the event amount is at least the order amount before marking the order and all its line items paid.

Buyer-triggered manual payment verification is a rate-limited ownership-checked fallback for missing or delayed webhooks; shared confirmation treats paid and later fulfillment statuses as already paid to avoid duplicate confirmation effects.

Gateway cancellation events invoke a service-role-only cancellation RPC which only cancels orders still awaiting payment and restores stock; manual seller/admin cancellation requires a reason, is forbidden after `Enviado`, restores stock, clears eligible payment flags, marks pending payout ledger entries reversed, and does not perform an Asaas refund.

The verified order-status vocabulary is `Aguardando Pagamento`, `Pagamento Realizado`, `Em Separação`, `Enviado`, and `Cancelado`; sellers or admins can only advance the linear paid-to-separation-to-sent progression through an authorized RPC.

Payment confirmation attempts WhatsApp notifications for the buyer's pickup/delivery code and seller's paid-order notice, buyer email, and delivery dispatch after persistence; these notification and routing side effects are best-effort and do not invalidate payment confirmation.

Delivery completion is stored per line in `entregas`, not as an additional order status; authenticated store/eligible logistics actors and a public carrier route can confirm a paid order with the buyer code, with idempotent success and incorrect-code attempt limits.

Confirmed delivery recalculates payout ledger entries, and the application then transfers pending eligible seller or affiliate payouts using Asaas PIX transfers; missing eligibility becomes `inelegivel`, transfer failures become `falhou`, and payout failure does not reverse delivery.
Focused unit tests cover checkout schema validation and allowed payment methods, freight rounding/fallback selection, constant-time token behavior, and notification email status content.
